title: Tops can hide any constraint problem
claim: (1) For every finite structure H and every q >= 2, the equal-top lift of H, on Z_q x (domain of H) with each relation of H required to have equal first coordinates in each atom, composes like cycles: in every system the free sets are exactly the sets with at most one visible variable in each component of the system's constraint hypergraph, a partition matroid. (2) The lift is homomorphically equivalent to H, so its core is the core of H. Hence the core of a law that composes like cycles need not compose like cycles (the lift of 3-colouring has core K3), laws composing like cycles can have non-Taylor cores (K3, not-all-equal) and NP-complete constraint problems, and every finite-template constraint problem is that of a law composing like cycles; with a constant added, the lift of 3-colouring violates elimination, as CYCLE-UTILITY-20261021-001A-P001 requires. (3) The shifted lift, which adds the relation 'the first coordinate goes up by one', also composes like cycles with the same partition matroid; its endomorphisms are the maps (a, s) -> (a + c, h_a(s)) with each h_a an endomorphism of H, so it is a core when H is; its constraint problem is polynomial-time equivalent to that of H, and it has a Siggers polymorphism only if H has one. So cores composing like cycles can be non-Taylor with NP-complete constraint problems (the shifted lifts of K3, not-all-equal and one-in-three), and composing like cycles does not imply polynomial time unless P = NP, even for cores. (4) A law that composes like cycles and is a core with no nontrivial automorphism pp-defines its constants, so its constraint problem is solvable in polynomial time; both hypotheses are needed (the equal-top and shifted lifts of one-in-three).
failure_conditions: A system of an equal-top or shifted lift has a free set with two visible variables in one component, or a constrained set with at most one per component.
The projection or the embedding is not a homomorphism, or the cores of the K3 and not-all-equal lifts differ from K3 and not-all-equal.
K3 or not-all-equal has a Siggers polymorphism.
The lift of 3-colouring with a constant satisfies elimination in the exhibited system.
A shifted lift of K3, not-all-equal or one-in-three has a non-bijective endomorphism, or a number of endomorphisms other than q times |Aut H| to the power q.
A shifted 3-colouring instance is satisfiable while the graph is not 3-colourable or its offsets are inconsistent, or the converse.
foundation_claim_scope: Composing like cycles and the complexity of constraint problems: tops can hide any constraint problem. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim, and no claim about P versus NP.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py samples 1,440 systems of twelve equal-top lifts (671 nonempty) and 720 systems of six shifted lifts (266 nonempty) against the partition-matroid prediction, computes the cores of the K3 and not-all-equal lifts and the endomorphisms of the shifted lifts, searches Siggers polymorphisms exhaustively (none for K3 or not-all-equal; found for the Z3 law and parity), checks the pinned system, 38 lifted and 60 shifted 3-colouring instances, and the rigid-core illustration; four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with randomized and exhaustive checks; the CSP dichotomy (Bulatov; Zhuk), the Siggers characterization of Taylor structures, the transfer of identities without nesting along homomorphisms, the NP-completeness of 3-colouring, not-all-equal and one-in-three, and CYCLE-UTILITY-20261021-001A-P001 are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta: both lifts are standard product constructions and their constraint problems are classical; new to the program is that they compose like cycles (a partition matroid of components), which settles the core question negatively, shows that being a core does not help, and bounds the positive remainder at rigid cores.
